candidates.name: Tax-free refund at Haneda T3 (new refund system)
candidates.name_ja: 免税リファンド方式・羽田空港第3ターミナル税関確認
candidates.why: From 1 Nov 2026 Japan stopped taking tax off at the till. You now pay the full price including the 10% tax, show your passport, and register how you want the refund paid. When you leave, you scan your passport at the customs tax-free kiosk in the departure lobby, or use Visit Japan Web on the airport's tax-free Wi-Fi, BEFORE you drop bags at the airline counter. GREEN means the refund is approved, and the shop or its refund operator pays it to the registered method (secondary guides say 1–2 weeks to a card). RED means a customs inspection. Rules: at least ¥5,000 before tax per store per day; customs must check you within 90 days; the old consumables cap and sealed bags are gone, but anything eaten or used in Japan isn't refunded; it's per receipt, so if one item on a receipt is missing, nothing on that receipt is refunded; only quantities you can carry out yourself.
candidates.best_time: Tue 29 Dec: aim to reach T3 by ~14:00 for the 17:20 flight. 29 Dec is a peak year-end departure day, and you must do the kiosk with all goods BEFORE bag drop, with no compensation if you run out of time.
candidates.dates: Applies to everything bought 15–29 Dec 2026 (all under the new system, no transition period)
candidates.price: Refund ≈10% of the tax-inclusive price; some operators deduct a fee. Don Quijote (PPIH) is fee-free unless you take cash at the airport
candidates.booking: Register on Visit Japan Web before arrival (speeds up both shops and the airport kiosk). At each tax-free shop, show your passport and register the refund method (card etc.).
candidates.group_of_8: Each person must buy and claim on their own passport. Don't pool purchases on one receipt across people. Pack every refundable item in an easy-to-reach bag so all 8 can clear the kiosk fast.
candidates.hours: Kiosks in the international departure lobby, before check-in/bag drop
candidates.first_last: Must be done before checking bags. Checked bags can't be retrieved for the procedure.

evidence.note: Refund method from 1 Nov 2026: pay tax-inclusive, ¥5,000 min per store per day, 90 days, kiosk before checked-baggage drop, green/red, per-receipt all-or-nothing, consumables used in Japan not refunded, packaging rule abolished

Traveller flow: buy tax-incl. → register refund method → kiosk (or VJW on airport Wi-Fi at Haneda/Narita/Kansai etc.) → airline bag drop → refund. ¥500k consumables cap and special packaging abolished

evidence.source: PPIH / Don Quijote press via Hokkaido Shimbun
evidence.note: From 1 Nov 2026 refund fee is free at all PPIH (Don Quijote) stores; operator fee applies only if refund is taken in cash at the airport
Joint customs/immigration kiosks in full operation at Haneda T2/T3 using Visit Japan Web QR + IC passport

candidates.name: MEGA Don Quijote Shibuya Main Store
candidates.name_ja: MEGAドン・キホーテ渋谷本店
candidates.why: The biggest 24-hour Donki in central Tokyo: snacks, KitKats, cosmetics, costumes, character goods and cheap electronics on several floors. Now that the refund system is in, Donki is the easy place for tax-free shopping, since PPIH waives the refund fee (unless you take cash at the airport). Go late at night after Shibuya, when it's the classic group outing.
candidates.best_time: After 22:00 on a Shibuya night, when the day crowds thin and nothing else is open for shopping. Avoid 17:00–20:00.
candidates.price: ¥3,000–10,000 pp typical haul; hit ¥5,000 ex-tax on ONE receipt per person for the refund
candidates.group_of_8: Fine. Split into pairs with a 30-min meet-up at the entrance; everyone pays separately on their own passport.

evidence.note: Open 24h, 4.2★ from ~22.8k reviews (Oct 2026)

evidence.source: PPIH press release via Hokkaido Shimbun
evidence.note: Fee-free tax refunds at all Don Quijote stores from 1 Nov 2026

candidates.name: Super Potato Retro-kan
candidates.name_ja: スーパーポテト レトロ館
candidates.why: The best-known retro game shop in Akihabara: three cramped floors of Famicom, Game Boy, PS1 and N64 stock, plus a small retro arcade on the top floor. It still goes viral on TikTok in 2026. Good for browsing and photos, but prices are collector level, so the Book-Off and Surugaya stores in the area are cheaper for actually buying games.
candidates.best_time: Weekday early afternoon; pair with Mandarake Complex and Radio Kaikan on one Akihabara loop
candidates.group_of_8: Floors are tight, so go in two groups of four.

candidates.name: Mandarake Complex + Radio Kaikan loop
candidates.name_ja: まんだらけコンプレックス／秋葉原ラジオ会館
candidates.why: These two are the core of an Akihabara shopping run. Mandarake Complex is an 8-floor secondhand tower: manga, figures, cels, idol goods and vintage toys. Radio Kaikan (by the station) has 10 floors of figure shops, card shops, gachapon and anime goods. Secondhand figures and cards cost far less than new, so it's a good budget pick.
candidates.best_time: From 12:00 (Mandarake opens at noon). Weekdays are calmer. Combine with Ueno/Ameyoko, 2 stops on the Yamanote line.
candidates.group_of_8: Split by interest (cards, figures, retro) and regroup at Radio Kaikan's front.

evidence.note: Mandarake Complex 4.2★ ~6.1k reviews, 12:00–20:00; Radio Kaikan 4.3★, 10:00–20:00 (Oct 2026)

candidates.name: Shibuya PARCO (Nintendo Tokyo, Pokémon Center Shibuya, Capcom, Jump Shop)

candidates.name: Koenji vintage crawl (Pal & Look arcades, Kita-Kore Building)
candidates.name_ja: 高円寺 古着（パル商店街・ルック商店街・キタコレビル）
candidates.why: Locals and 2025–26 Xiaohongshu guides now prefer Koenji to Shimokitazawa for vintage. There are more shops, a wider range of styles, rougher edges, fewer tourists and generally lower prices. Walk south from Koenji Station down Pal into Look arcade toward Shin-Koenji, then cross to the north side for Kita-Kore Building's punk and designer-archive shops. It's 6 minutes from Shinjuku on the Chuo line, so it works well during the Garfield House stay.
candidates.best_time: Start 12:00 or later; most shops open at noon and the area is dead in the morning. Pair with Nakano Broadway one stop away.
candidates.dates: 26–28 Dec work. Some indie shops close irregularly over the New Year, so check the shop's Instagram.
candidates.group_of_8: Shops are tiny, so split into 2–3 groups, use the arcade as the spine and meet at the station.

evidence.note: Sep 2026: 'buy vintage in Koenji', 8 must-visit shops, more varied than Shimokitazawa

candidates.name: Nakano Broadway
candidates.why: A 1960s arcade building whose floors 2–4 are packed with Mandarake branches and small collector shops: figures, retro toys, idol goods, watches, cards. It's calmer and often cheaper than Akihabara. It's one Chuo-line stop from Koenji, so the two make a perfect afternoon.
candidates.best_time: After Koenji, from ~15:00; most shops open around noon and close at 20:00
candidates.group_of_8: Narrow corridors; go in two groups.

evidence.note: Anime-themed shops as a relaxed alternative to Akihabara

candidates.name: Shimokitazawa vintage (Flamingo, New York Joe Exchange, reload)
candidates.name_ja: 下北沢 古着（フラミンゴ・ニューヨークジョーエクスチェンジ・reload）
candidates.why: Tokyo's best-known vintage village. Flamingo is the classic American-vintage shop. New York Joe Exchange is a former bathhouse used as a trade-in thrift, with the cheapest racks in the area. reload is the new low-rise mall along the old rail line, with curated shops and cafés. Recent Chinese and Reddit reviews say the main streets are pricier and more touristy than they were, so dig the side streets and bargain racks, or do Koenji if you only have time for one.
candidates.best_time: 12:00–17:00, then 4 min on the Inokashira line to Shibuya for the evening
candidates.price: ¥1,000–3,000 at NY Joe; ¥3,000–10,000 per piece at curated shops
candidates.group_of_8: Compact area, easy to split and regroup at reload.

candidates.name: Harajuku → Ura-Hara → Cat Street walk (atmos, Kicks Lab, 2nd Street)
candidates.name_ja: 原宿・裏原宿・キャットストリート
candidates.why: The streetwear and sneaker spine of Tokyo. Do Takeshita Street quickly at opening (crepes, cheap accessories), cross Meiji-dori into Ura-Hara's back lanes (brand flagships, consignment such as L.A. Avenue), then walk Cat Street south to Shibuya. On the way you pass atmos and Kicks Lab for sneakers, plus 2nd Street and Kinji for budget secondhand. The route ends at Shibuya PARCO and Miyashita Park.
candidates.best_time: Takeshita at 10:00–11:00 before it jams; Ura-Hara/Cat Street 11:30–16:00; finish in Shibuya at dusk
candidates.booking: Hyped sneaker drops at atmos/Kicks Lab use raffles in apps or on Instagram. Check a week ahead.
candidates.group_of_8: Takeshita is shoulder-to-shoulder, so set one meet point (Harajuku station, Omotesando exit).

candidates.name: Isetan Shinjuku depachika
candidates.name_ja: 伊勢丹新宿店 食品館（デパ地下）
candidates.why: Isetan Shinjuku's basement food floor, the best-known department-store food hall in Tokyo: wagashi, high-end sweets in gift boxes, bento and sake. candidates.name: Nakameguro Koukashita & Daikanyama
candidates.name_ja: 中目黒高架下・代官山
candidates.why: Honest verdict: lowest priority for this group. Nakameguro and Daikanyama are pretty and grown-up: select shops, antique vintage like JANTIQUES, Traveler's Factory, Daikanyama T-Site and Log Road. They're priced for 30-somethings and there's little in December to justify the trip. Do it only if you have a spare half-day; it's one stop from Shibuya on the Tokyu Toyoko line, and you can walk Daikanyama → Nakameguro in 10 minutes.
candidates.best_time: 14:00–19:00, ending at dusk under the Koukashita tracks

evidence.note: Koukashita strip under the tracks has vintage shops; Daikanyama 10 min walk

notes: Tokyo · shop: AREA LOGIC (Tokyo shopping). Stay 1, 15–19 Dec, Ninja House/Ikebukuro: arrival evening = animate flagship, Otome Road, Sunshine City/Pokémon Center Mega Tokyo, then the Ikebukuro Donki. Do an east-side day: Akihabara (Mandarake Complex, Radio Kaikan, Super Potato) + Ueno Ameyoko/mita sneakers, 2 Yamanote stops apart. Do Ameyoko in this first stay, because from 28 Dec it becomes a New Year food-market crush. Do Tokyo Station souvenirs (Character Street/Okashi Land) here too, if they fit. Stay 2, 26–29 Dec, Garfield House/Shinjuku: West day = Koenji (from 12:00) → Nakano Broadway, both on the Chuo line 6 min from Shinjuku. South day = Takeshita at 10:00 → Ura-Hara → Cat Street on foot → Shibuya PARCO/Miyashita Park; or Shimokitazawa 12:00–17:00 → Inokashira line 4 min → Shibuya, then MEGA Donki late. Nakameguro/Daikanyama is optional and low value for this budget. The Yamanote and Chuo lines cover all of it, so use IC cards (Suica/PASMO), no pass needed. YEAR-END: department stores and malls should keep normal hours 26–30 Dec (31 Dec shortened, 1 Jan closed). But the big winter sales and 初売り start 2 Jan (Isetan, Lumine) or 3 Jan (PARCO Grand Bazaar), after the 29 Dec flight, so malls are full price. Get value from secondhand (Koenji, NY Joe, 2nd Street, Mandarake) and Donki instead. Depachika are packed on 28–30 Dec with osechi shoppers. Some small vintage shops close irregularly around New Year, so check their Instagram. TAX-FREE (from 1 Nov 2026): pay full price incl. 10% tax, show your passport, and register the refund method. Keep ≥¥5,000 ex-tax on one receipt per shop per day, per person. Don't eat or use what you'll claim, and keep the whole receipt's items together. At Haneda T3 on 29 Dec, do the customs kiosk (or Visit Japan Web on airport Wi-Fi) with all goods BEFORE bag drop. Arrive by ~14:00 for the 17:20 flight on this peak departure day. Donki waives the refund fee unless you take cash at the airport.
